newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral under pressure to jettison old boss.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral under pressure to jettison old boss.

text.p: A split in his own party has thrown up the toughest challenge yet for Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's stewardship of his two-month-old minority coalition government, political analysts said on Tuesday.
Gujral faced pressure from his left-wing allies to recommend the dismissal of former party boss, Laloo Prasad Yadav, the popular chief minister of the esatern state of Bihar.
"We want Laloo Prasad to step down as chief minister," D. Raja, a senior leader of Communist Party of India (CPI), told Reuters.
"We can decide later whether Laloo Yadav can be included in the coalition or not," Raja said.
A powerful dissident group on Saturday broke away from the Janata Dal party under the leadership of its former president Yadav, who has been indicted in a corruption scandal.
Yadav said he would continue to support the centre-left government, where three of his supporters are ministers.
"I have no intention to remove the three ministers," Gujral was quoted by Press Trust of India (PTI) as saying in an interview to a private television channel.
Gujral is under pressure from left allies to bid a good bye to Yadav who has charged by the federal police in the $280 million embezzlement case.
The left parties are meeting in the Indian capital on Tuesday to chalk out a strategy to deal with the current political crisis facing the fractious 15-party coalition.
Yadav says he is innocent of the charges and has rejected calls from alliance partners to step down.
"Gujral has a problem on his hand. He seems to unwilling to bell the Laloo Prasad cat," political analyst Rasheed Talib told Reuters.
The Congress party, which provides crucial make-or-break support to Gujral's government, can also flex its muscles with an eye on dislodging the alliance.
Gujral must look over his shoulder for any moves by the main opposition Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) to take of advantage, political analysts said.
The BJP emerged as the single largest party with 162 deputies in the 545-seat parliament after an inconclusive general election in May last year.
The Hindu nationalists have urged President Shankar Dayal Sharma to dismiss Yadav as Bihar chief minister and launched a massive political campaign in the state.
